finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the input contains format specifiers (e.g., %s, %n), it could lead to arbitrary code execution.
finding.assumptions: The attacker can control the input data received from the client, which is then printed using printf.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the printf statement at line 50; the format string is the constant literal "%02x " and the only argument supplied is an unsigned char cast of buffer[i]. No untrusted data is used as the format string itself, so no format‑string or command‑injection vulnerability exists. No other path from the untrusted source to a format string sink was found.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the received data is larger than the buffer size, it could lead to a buffer overflow.
finding.assumptions: The attacker can control the input data size, and the buffer is fixed in size.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code uses recvfrom(server_socket, buffer, sizeof(buffer), ...). The third argument limits the number of bytes written to buffer to sizeof(buffer) (258). Therefore the buffer cannot be overrun by recvfrom. The subsequent loop prints only up to received_bytes, which is guaranteed <= sizeof(buffer). No other writes to buffer occur. Thus there is no path from the untrusted source to an unsafe write or format that could overflow the buffer.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the input contains format specifiers (e.g., %s, %n), it could lead to arbitrary code execution.
finding.assumptions: The attacker can control the input data received from the client, which is then sent back to the client.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Searched for any path where the untrusted buffer is passed to a function that interprets format specifiers or executes shell commands. The only sink is sendto, which transmits raw bytes over UDP and does not evaluate the data. No format string usage or system call is invoked with the buffer content. Thus the reported OS Command Injection claim is unfounded.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the received data is larger than the buffer size, it could lead to a buffer overflow.
finding.assumptions: The attacker can control the input data size, and the buffer is fixed in size.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that recvfrom writes at most sizeof(buffer) bytes (line 41), thus no overflow from received data. The subsequent sendto uses buffer contents read from stdin via fgets (line 58) which also respects buffer size, preventing overflow. No path from an untrusted source to a dangerous operation without size checks. No trigger can cause a buffer overflow.
